newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt should rethink cuts - Opp'n.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt should rethink cuts - Opp'n.

text.p: Australian Opposition Treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said on Friday the government should reconsider its budget strategy given the widening of this month's current account deficit.
The current account deficit, seasonally adjusted, widened to A$1.788 billion in October from A$1.690 billion the previous month, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said.
Evans said: "If anything, today's figures highlight just how wrong the government is to be hacking into programmes that help our manufacturers export and compete in world markets."
"Merchandise export growth has slowed to a crawl," Evans said in a statement.

The Liberal-National government announced a tough budget for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), slashing spending by A$3.9 billion and halving the underlying deficit to A$5.6 billion from A$10.3 billion in 1995/96.
